pending_commit.commit_message: nebraska: Add options to write port, pid, and log into specific files. - Add --runtime-root flag so users can specify a directory where we write these two files into: * port - To specify the port nebraska is serving, so a remote caller can use this port value to send request to nebraska. * pid - To specify the pid of the nebraska, so a remote caller can gracefully kill the nebraska using this pid value. - Add --log-file flag to specify a file for nebraska to write the logs into. If not passed it logs into stdout/stderr. We need to log to a specific file so after the update/install process was finished/failed, we can copy the log back and looking at it for debugging purposes. We should not log into syslog as it gets messed up with the other logs in the system and it makes it very hard to debug things. There are a lot of XML requests/responses that are generated by the nebraska and it is ideal for us to be able to look at the log all by itself and figure out what went wrong. nebraska: Break --payload-addr into two flags Currently, the nebraska adds /update or /install to the --payload-addr flag based on whether the request is install or update. But this is unfair to the server/service that serves the payload. They have to change their code semantics in order to handle this. Even more complicated we send an Omaha request to a devserver address like: "http://devserver-address/update" so the devserver so can send a response back. Now adding /update or /install to the end of addresses like this can become more confusing and cumbersome. So instead of nebraska making such assumptions, we should directly pass the addresses for install and updates to nebraska. If no address for install was passed we use the update address instead. So flag --payload-addr was replaced by two flags --update-payloads-address and --install-payloads-address. kukui: Pulse PMIC_FORCE_RESET_ODL on external reset If the reset cause is external, it is wise to reset the PMIC registers, which can be achieved by pulsing the force reset signal to PMIC. We found in previous experiments that 5ms is often enough to reset the PMIC, but that occasionally the PMIC would auto-restart if the pulse is so short (so we pulse for 10s when we force shutdown the AP). Here, we pulse for 100ms, which is an acceptable delay in these situations, and hopefully long enough to recover from bad PMIC settings. CHROMIUM: media: rockchip-vpu: Clear read cache before decoding The VDEC IP block includes a read cache, which is not coherent with writes coming out of the same block or from any other bus masters, including the CPU. Moreover, the cache is IOVA addressed, so when another buffer ends up mapped at the same IOVA, the cache could have stale entries for the old buffer. To fix the issue, the cache needs to be cleared. Ideally we would do that only if the buffer is dirty or a remap happened. However, clearing every frame did not lead to any performance effect above the measurement error, so let's just keep it simple. [githooks] Add a test runner This CL adds a test-runner as ./run_tests_for.py. This can manually be invoked pretty easily; just hand it a few files, and it'll try to figure out what tests need to be run for that. If it finds any tests, they'll be run in parallel. This includes an incidental update to our yapf style, per reviewer comments. The intent is to use this script to run tests as part of a `repo upload` hook. Test discovery is kind of haphazard, and split into two phases. Basically, there's a set of directories where if you touch anything in that directory, all tests in that directory get run (see `_find_forced_subdir_tests`). Otherwise, this script just tries to find names of files similar to the ones it's given, but with _test/_unittest in them. I chose this method of discovery since `foo_unittest.py` and `foo_test.py` appear to be the two prevalent naming conventions here, and no one wants to keep a text file (or similar) up-to-date with all of the tests that exist. At the moment, this only supports Python. Adding support for auto-detecting other tests should hopefully be straightforward enough, if we want to add it. BUG=None TEST=Ran crosperf's tests.
